prompt.context_jp: 「私は ＭＥＲ計画を潰したいの」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___ ＭＥＲ計画を潰したいの」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this topic-marking, personal-stance statement.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is declaring her own stance as the topic of discussion — 'As for me, I want to crush it.' は frames 私 as the known theme and sets up her position.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 私 as new/exhaustive information ('It's I who want to crush it'), which doesn't fit — she's confiding her stance, not identifying herself among candidates.

contrast_examples.jp: 私はコーヒーが好きです。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, I like coffee. (topic)
I'll be the one to do it. (exhaustive/identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 拠点の空気が一変したのは、その直後だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 拠点の空気___一変したのは、その直後だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that fits inside the 〜のは cleft.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜のは... clause, the subject usually takes が. The focus (new info) is 'その直後' — the embedded event '空気が一変した' is backgrounded.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this nominalized clause would try to make a second topic, clashing with the main-clause topic marked by のは.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降ったのは昨日です。
contrast_examples.en: It was yesterday that it rained.
When he came, I was surprised. (subordinate が)

prompt.context_jp: 天井のスピーカーから警告音が鳴り響き、目黒の張り詰めた声が流れ出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 天井のスピーカーから警告音___鳴り響き、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks this suddenly-appearing sound?

feedback.correct_en: A warning sound suddenly erupts — this is classic new-information が, presenting an event the reader didn't know about.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 警告音 as an already-established topic, but the sound is being introduced for the first time.

contrast_examples.jp: その電話は father からだった。
contrast_examples.en: That phone call was from Dad. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「大事なのは 目の前の命です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大事___のは 目の前の命です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this cleft 〜のは construction?

feedback.correct_en: 大事 is a na-adjective, so modifying こと/の takes な: 大事なのは. The whole phrase then becomes the topic, with 命 as the exhaustive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大事が would try to use 大事 as a noun subject, which doesn't fit the fixed cleft pattern 〜なのは〜です.

prompt.context_jp: 「お前とは立場が違うんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お前と___ 立場が違うんだよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle Komaba uses to contrast his position with Kitami's.

feedback.correct_en: 〜とは marks a contrastive topic: 'As for compared with you, my position is different.' は after と pointedly separates the two.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜とが isn't a natural pairing here; と already marks the comparison partner, and the discourse needs the contrastive emphasis of は.

prompt.context_jp: それでも喜多見の背中は、いつもと同じ穏やかさで揺らがなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも喜多見の背中___、いつもと同じ穏やかさで揺らがなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the contrast with everyone else's fear.

feedback.correct_en: それでも signals contrast with Hina's fear in the preceding sentence. は highlights Kitami's back as the contrastive theme — unlike the others, his was unshaken.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present his back as new information, losing the explicit contrast that それでも sets up.

contrast_examples.jp: みんな慌てたが、彼は落ち着いていた。
contrast_examples.en: Everyone panicked, but he was calm. (contrast は)

contrast_examples.jp: 誰かが落ち着いていた。

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見の判断は瞬時だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見の判断___ 瞬時だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best fits this characterizing statement?

feedback.correct_en: This is a characterizing (thetic→categorical) statement about 喜多見の判断 — 'his judgment was instantaneous.' は sets up the already-established referent as the topic being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like a sudden new discovery; but Kitami's actions are the ongoing topic, so は is the natural choice.

prompt.context_jp: 頭上でひときわ大きな金属音が響き渡る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭上でひときわ大きな金属音___響き渡る。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this suddenly-appearing dramatic sound?

feedback.correct_en: A loud metallic sound bursts into the scene — new-information が introduces the dramatic event the characters (and reader) just became aware of.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the sound as previously-established topic, but the sound is the shocking new event itself.

prompt.context_jp: 彼女にとってこの拠点は、まだどこか居心地の悪い場所だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女にとってこの拠点___、まだどこか居心地の悪い場所だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up this characterizing description of 'this base'?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is describing 'this base' as the topic Hina feels uncomfortable in — a stable property stated about a known referent. は is the natural topic marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the base as new/exhaustive info, but it's already in the scene; the sentence is characterizing it from her perspective.

contrast_examples.en: Oh, a room is open. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 誰も巻き込まれていない——その一言に、駒場は肩の力を抜いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰___ 巻き込まれていない
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that forms the natural 'nobody' negative construction.

feedback.correct_en: 誰も + negative = 'no one at all.' This is the standard pattern for universal negation in Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical as a bare phrase — 誰 (who) must pair with か (someone) or も (anyone/no one), not with topic は.

prompt.context_jp: 大きな声で仲間を呼び集めるその姿には、上下関係を意識する素振りは微塵もない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大きな声で仲間___呼び集める
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the people being called together?

feedback.correct_en: 呼び集める is a transitive verb ('gather/summon'). 仲間 is the direct object being gathered, so を is correct.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination/goal ('call out TO comrades'), but 呼び集める takes the group as a direct object, not a target.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見は身を低くして、クレーンの真下へと潜り込んでいった。
prompt.prompt_jp: クレーンの真下___潜り込んでいった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the destination of 潜り込む?

feedback.correct_en: 潜り込む takes a destination with へ/に. The literary 〜へと emphasizes directional motion toward 'right under the crane.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks a location where an action occurs, not a direction/goal, so でと is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: その口調はどこまでも柔らかく、恐怖に凍りついた表情をわずかに緩めていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その口調___ どこまでも柔らかく、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle characterizes 'that tone' here?

feedback.correct_en: その口調 refers back to Kitami's already-described voice — a known, anaphoric topic. は picks up this topic and asserts a quality about it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would newly introduce 'a tone,' but we already know whose tone it is; the sentence is describing the known theme.

prompt.context_jp: 頭上の鉄骨が、微かな軋みを立てて揺れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭上の鉄骨___、微かな軋みを立てて揺れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this sudden event description?

feedback.correct_en: The steel beam swaying is a new, startling event in the narrative — new-information が presents the whole event as freshly observed.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 鉄骨 as the known topic being commented on, but here the point is the sudden movement, not a general property of the beam.

prompt.context_jp: 「TOKYO MERは 都知事直轄の医療組織です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「TOKYO MER___ 都知事直轄の医療組織です」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this definitional X=Y announcement?

feedback.correct_en: This is a definitional/characterizing statement: 'As for TOKYO MER, it is a medical organization under the governor.' は sets up the topic to be defined.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be identificational ('It's TOKYO MER that is...'), implying contrast with other candidates — but the governor is simply explaining what MER is.

prompt.context_jp: 「皆さーん これ 自分の名前 書いてください」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「皆さーん これ 自分の名前 ___ ください」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb form fits Kitami's casual request to write names on duct tape?

feedback.correct_en: 〜てください = polite request. 書いて is the te-form of 書く, needed to form 書いてください ('please write').
feedback.incorrect_en: 書けて is potential te-form ('being able to write'), and 書かれて is passive — neither forms a request. Only plain te-form combines with ください.

contrast_examples.jp: 名前を書いてください。

prompt.context_jp: 気胸を疑い、胸腔ドレーンの準備を仲間に告げる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気胸を___、胸腔ドレーンの準備を仲間に告げる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits the medical reasoning 'suspecting pneumothorax'?

feedback.correct_en: 疑う = to suspect/doubt. In medical contexts, 〜を疑う means 'to suspect (a diagnosis),' which is exactly what Kitami is doing with pneumothorax.
feedback.incorrect_en: 信じる ('believe') and 願う ('wish') don't fit diagnostic reasoning. A doctor doesn't 'believe in' or 'wish for' a condition — they suspect it.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見は千住の制止をやんわりと受け流し、麻酔の針を構えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見は千住の制止をやんわりと ___、麻酔の針を構えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb captures how Kitami handles Senju's objection?

feedback.correct_en: 受け流す = to parry/deflect/let slide. やんわりと受け流す means 'gently brush aside,' which fits Kitami ignoring Senju's protest without confrontation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 受け止める means 'take seriously / catch,' which would mean he accepted the warning. 受け取る is just 'receive (an item).' Both lose the deflection nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「虎穴に入らずんば ___ を得ず」
prompt.prompt_en: Complete this classical proverb Min quotes.

feedback.correct_en: The fixed proverb is 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず — 'If you don't enter the tiger's den, you won't get the tiger cub.' Both halves must reference 虎.
feedback.incorrect_en: 宝物 or 成功 would convey the general meaning but break the set phrase. Proverbs must be reproduced verbatim to count as the idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず。

contrast_examples.en: Fall seven times, stand up eight.

prompt.context_jp: それでも喜多見は諦めるという選択肢を頭から締め出し、次の一手を口にした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見は諦めるという選択肢を頭から ___、次の一手を口にした。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'shut out the option from his mind'?

feedback.correct_en: 締め出す = shut out / lock out. 頭から締め出す ('shut out of one's mind') is the natural collocation for refusing to consider something.
feedback.incorrect_en: 取り出す ('take out') and 引き出す ('draw out') move something OUT to use it — the opposite of banishing it from thought.

contrast_examples.jp: 不安を頭から締め出す。
contrast_examples.en: Shut anxiety out of one's mind.

prompt.context_jp: 「何より責任を逃れることは 組織で生き残る 最善の道ですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「責任を ___ ことは 組織で生き残る 最善の道ですから」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb forms the standard collocation with 責任?

feedback.correct_en: 責任を逃れる is the fixed collocation for 'escape/evade responsibility.' 逃れる takes を directly with abstract obligations.
feedback.incorrect_en: 責任から逃げる works but needs から, not を. 離れる ('to be apart from') doesn't fit the abstract 'evade' meaning Otowa is cynically describing.

prompt.context_jp: 自分が他の人より偉いと思うような振る舞いを一切見せない喜多見に、皆はいつしか引き寄せられていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆はいつしか ___ ていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which form fits 'everyone is gradually drawn to him'?

feedback.correct_en: The team is BEING drawn in by Kitami's attitude — passive 引き寄せられる. 〜ていく adds the gradual-unfolding nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: Active 引き寄せ would mean 'they are drawing (something) in,' and causative 引き寄せさせ would mean 'making X draw it in' — neither matches the attracted-to-him sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 磁石に引き寄せられる。

prompt.context_jp: しかし比奈は、その疑いを口にすることを躊躇った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 比奈は、その疑いを ___ ことを躊躇った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which collocation means 'put her suspicion into words'?

feedback.correct_en: 口にする = to put into words / to voice. 疑いを口にする = 'to voice one's suspicion' — the natural idiom here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口を出す = 'to butt in' (interfere), 口が立つ = 'to be eloquent.' Neither means 'to say out loud what one is thinking.'

prompt.context_jp: 「死者ゼロって… 無理でしょ ここでオペなんて無理です！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as an exasperated casual-polite outburst in this scene?

choices.text: 死者ゼロって… 無理でしょ ここでオペなんて無理です！
死者ゼロということは… 不可能であろう ここで手術などすることは不可能です！

feedback.correct_en: The original uses natural spoken rhythm: casual 〜って quotation, 無理でしょ with falling intonation, and emphatic なんて. It conveys shock from a medical professional in a tense moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically correct but reads like formal written Japanese (〜であろう, 不可能) — far too stiff for a doctor's live reaction at a disaster scene.

contrast_examples.en: No way, this is impossible. (natural spoken)

prompt.context_jp: 「圧迫が続く状態は危険です お名前って言えますか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural when a doctor gently asks a trapped child her name?

choices.text: お名前って言えますか？
御芳名を申告していただけますでしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: お名前って言えますか is softly polite but accessible — the colloquial 〜って and simple 言えますか let a scared child answer easily.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses extreme business/legal keigo (御芳名, 申告) that would frighten or confuse a trapped middle-schooler. Register must match the listener.

contrast_examples.en: Can you tell me your name? (gentle)

contrast_examples.jp: 御芳名をお聞かせください。
contrast_examples.en: May I hear your esteemed name? (overly formal)

prompt.context_jp: 「待ってる時間がありません 夏梅さん 麻酔 いきますよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is more natural for Kitami's quick command to his team mid-emergency?

choices.text: 待ってる時間がありません。夏梅さん、麻酔いきますよ。
待っている時間が存在しない状況でございますので、夏梅様、麻酔を開始させていただきます。

feedback.correct_en: A matches the clipped, team-leader rhythm of medical fieldwork: short clauses, 〜ますよ to prompt action, 〜さん with colleagues.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is comically over-polite for a critical medical moment. 〜様 for a teammate and 〜させていただきます would waste precious seconds and sound wrong.

contrast_examples.jp: 開始させていただきます。

prompt.context_jp: 「でも そうなら 先に言ってくれればいいのに マジ 焦りましたよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches Tokumaru's casual griping about Kitami?

choices.text: 先に言ってくれればいいのに、マジ焦りましたよ。
事前にお伝えいただければ幸いでしたのに、誠に動揺いたしました。

feedback.correct_en: A fits Tokumaru's casual-colleague register: 〜てくれればいいのに (mild complaint) and マジ as an intensifier are what young staff say to peers after a crisis.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is formal business email register (〜いただければ幸い, 誠に動揺) — totally wrong for teammates chatting after work in a break room.

contrast_examples.jp: 誠に動揺いたしました。

prompt.context_jp: 「言いたいことがあるなら はっきり 言ってください！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version better captures Hina's emotional outburst at Otowa?

choices.text: 言いたいことがあるなら、はっきり言ってください！
もし御発言すべき事柄が存在するのであれば、明確に御表明くださいませ。

feedback.correct_en: A is a direct emotional challenge: 〜なら conditional + はっきり言ってください delivers urgency and frustration naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: B piles on overblown keigo (御発言, 御表明くださいませ) that drains all emotion. A character on the verge of tears doesn't reach for ceremonial polite forms.
